newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ORLANDO PIRATES FALL IN QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ORLANDO PIRATES FALL IN QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Holders Orlando Pirates became the latest victims of the African Champions' Cup curse, when they were knocked out in the quarter-finals at the weekend.

Their penalty shootout defeat by Shooting Stars of Nigeria in Ibadan on Saturday sees the South African team join a 27-year-long list of defending champions who have been unsuccessful in retaining Africa's top club prize.
Not since Zairean club TP Englebert retained the African Champion's Cup in 1968 has a team been able to win the competition in successive years.
Pirates hopes were shattered when Brendan Silent missed the vital kick in the shootout after a 1-1 aggregate draw.
The match was one of 11 African club competition quarter-final, second leg ties played at the weekend.
The holders travelled to Nigeria with a slim 1-0 lead after the first leg in Bloemfontein two weeks ago and lost the advantage after 55 minutes when Dotin Alatishe scored.

But it was Stars' goalkeeper Abiodun Baruwa who was the hero of the afternoon with two shootout saves and a penalty of his own to see the Nigerians through 4-3 on kicks to a semifinal meeting with Algeria's JS Kabylie.
Kabylie, last year's African Cup Winners' Cup victors, beat Angola's Petro Atletco 1-0 on Friday to advance 2-1 on aggregate.
The other Champions' Cup semifinal will involve Zamalek of Egypt, who beat COD Meknes of Morocco 4-2 on aggregate, against CS Sfaxien of Tunisia.
The Tunisian team went through despite losing 3-1 away at Diaraf Dakar on Sunday with all the goals coming in a furious first half.
Arab Contractors justified their billing as favourites in the African Cup Winners' Cup by reaching the semifinals at the expense of Moroccan opposition FUS Rabat.
Contractors won the second leg on Friday 1-0 after a goalless draw in the first leg earlier this month.
They now meet another former winner Canon Yaounde, who scored two vital away goals in a 2-2 draw away at Costa do Sol of Mozambique to progress on the away goals rule.
CAF Cup holders Etoile du Sahel conceded a last minute goal against Unisport Bafang in Cameroon on Sunday but still won 4-2 on aggregate to book their berth in the final four.
The Tunisian club will now have to travel further south in the semifinal where they meet Vita Club of Zaire.
Zaire's immensely popular team came from two goals behind to beat Mouloudia Oran of Algeria on post-match penalties in Kinshasa on Sunday.

The other semifinal clash pits Kenya Breweries, who ended Ports Authroty's dream of becoming the first club from Sierra Leone to reach the semifinal of any African club competition, against Kawkab Marrakesh of Morrocco.
